title: Till Guidance: Spending More than One Upgrade Credit on a Single Sale
content:
Where a customer holds several credits under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes, no more of them may be spent on one sale than the programme allows, and each credit is spent from its own registration. Credits from different programmes are never merged into one figure, and the customer chooses which to spend first when more than one could be spent.

## How a credit's position is read

What has been spent from a credit is read as the sum of the spends booked to that registration, taken over the whole life of the registration from the day the credit was issued to the handling date. The remaining credit is the credit issued less that sum plus any revaluation. After each spend, the credit remaining on the registration is the credit remaining before it less the amount of that spend.

## Where the customer wishes to spend more than the programme allows

Where the credits the customer wishes to spend exceed the programme's ceiling for one sale, the excess stays on its registration and may be spent on a later sale while it is still live. The number of credits a programme lets go on one sale, whether its credit may be spent in parts and whether it may sit alongside a promotional discount are the programme's published figures.

## Worked reading on hypothetical figures

A customer holds two registrations, one with 1200 USD issued and one with 800 USD issued, and wishes to spend both on a single sale under a programme that allows one credit on one sale. One credit is spent, chosen by the customer; the other stays on its own registration and may be spent on a later sale while it is still live. The two figures are never added into a single 2000 USD credit.

Suppose instead that the 1200 USD credit had been revalued upward by 100 USD and 300 USD had already been spent from it. Its remaining credit is 1200 USD less 300 USD plus 100 USD, which is 1000 USD; a further spend of 250 USD would leave 750 USD.
